sections.heading: In plain words
sections.body:
Still sends no analytics, usage events, advertising identifiers, automatic crash reports or viewing history to its developer. There is no Still account or preconfigured developer cloud service. Local video-link receiving needs no backend; optional whole-screen sharing uses the connection service you configure. Your settings stay on this device; your queue and pairing session stay in memory. This is what “zero developer telemetry” means in this app.

Playing online video necessarily contacts the chosen media provider. YouTube, Google, a stream host, your operating system and your network may process information under their own policies. This policy does not claim that online playback is anonymous or that no network traffic exists.

sections.heading: 1. Who is responsible and what this covers
sections.body:
Still is developed by muneebwanee, reachable at https://github.com/muneebwanee. This policy covers the Still iPhone/iPad app, its bundled local browser remote the Android Sender companion, optional connection-service source, and app-controlled data processing. It applies to this version from the effective date above. It does not govern GitHub, Apple, YouTube, browsers, routers or independently operated video sources.

The local-link mode does not send playback activity to an app server. Optional screen sharing necessarily sends negotiation and connection metadata to your selected operator; it is not an analytics upload. If you voluntarily contact the developer or publicly post an issue, the information you choose to provide is processed by the contact platform and may become public. Never include a pairing link or private media URL in a public report.

sections.heading: 2. Information stored on your device
sections.body:
Still stores small preferences in iOS UserDefaults: onboarding completion, receiver name, appearance and color theme, compact-layout and haptic choices, screen-awake and auto-next preferences, skip interval, stream quality, repeat and speed preferences, queue-only mode whether YouTube playback is allowed, background stream-audio preference, and the optional screen-sharing service address. These preferences are not a watch history and are not automatically sent to the developer.

During use, memory holds the current media URL and title, video ID where relevant, pending queue, playback position and duration, player volume and state, sleep-timer deadline, a local network address, the temporary pairing token and the time of the most recent accepted remote command. Queue and session information are not intentionally written to a persistent history database. User-provided titles and receiver names can themselves contain personal information, so avoid sensitive names when sharing a session.

sections.heading: 3. Information Still does not collect for telemetry
sections.body:
Still has no analytics SDK, advertising SDK, tracking pixel, fingerprinting service, developer crash-reporting upload, telemetry endpoint or account identifier. It does not sell personal information, build advertising profiles, run advertisements of its own, or combine activity across applications for advertising. There is no developer-side viewing database to export or delete.

This promise concerns app-authored collection. Apple may receive diagnostics according to your device and App Store settings. Your browser or operating system may maintain independent logs, network records, backups or security reports. Still cannot change those settings or represent that such system records do not exist.

sections.heading: 4. Local pairing and people on your network
sections.body:
Starting the receiver advertises Still’s own Bonjour service on Wi-Fi and opens a local HTTP listener. The displayed QR code contains a device address and a temporary random token. The token grants access to the local remote API until receiving stops. It changes on restart, on disconnecting all remotes, and after local wipe. No pairing information is sent to a developer server.

A paired remote can see the current title, source, playback status, timeline, player volume, queue titles and playback error. In full-control mode it can replace, queue, pause, resume, seek, stop or skip videos and change player volume. In queue-only mode it can read session status and add videos, while the receiver rejects transport and replacement commands. Queue-only is not a confidentiality boundary: paired users can still see titles and status.

Local remote traffic uses HTTP and is not encrypted. The token is an access credential, not encryption. A person intercepting your network traffic or obtaining the complete pairing link may control the receiver. Use trusted private Wi-Fi. Do not forward its listening port to the internet. Disconnect all remotes or stop the receiver when access should end.

sections.heading: 5. Online media and YouTube
sections.body:
Direct-stream playback connects the receiving device to the URL you choose and possibly to hosts referenced by its media playlist. Such hosts may receive your IP address, request headers, media URL, access tokens included in the URL, timestamps, device or playback information and other network metadata. The browser remote sends the link to Still; Still does not proxy the video through its developer.

YouTube playback uses the official iframe API and privacy-enhanced embed host in a nonpersistent WKWebView data store. Loading the player and playing a video contacts YouTube/Google services, including their API and media hosts. They may receive your IP address, video identifier, device/browser information, playback events and other information under Google’s Privacy Policy at https://policies.google.com/privacy and YouTube’s terms at https://www.youtube.com/t/terms. Privacy-enhanced mode does not eliminate provider processing. Provider ads or cookies may be involved according to provider behavior and applicable rules.

You can disable YouTube playback in Privacy & Data. This stops a current YouTube video and removes queued YouTube entries; new YouTube loads are rejected while disabled. This control does not block network requests made by direct media sources, nor does it erase records already held by providers.

sections.heading: 6. Permissions and device features
sections.body:
Still requests Local Network permission when you start receiving, for Bonjour advertisement and local commands. iOS decides whether and when to display the permission request. Denial can be changed in iOS Settings. The receiving iOS app does not request camera, microphone, photos, location, contacts, notifications or App Tracking Transparency authorization.

The receiving device displays a QR code; your other device scans it using its own camera or browser. Sharing a pairing link, document or support summary uses the system share sheet only after you choose to share. Still can keep the screen awake during an active session if you enable that preference. It releases that request when stopped or backgrounded. Optional haptics use supported device hardware without collecting interaction statistics.

sections.heading: 7. Retention, caches and local wipe
sections.body:
Preferences remain until changed, wiped or removed with the app, subject to operating-system backup and restore behavior. The queue, timer and current session are memory-only app state. Stopping the receiver revokes its token and closes its connections; backgrounding also ends whole-screen reception and pauses YouTube. Native direct-stream audio or Picture in Picture may continue when enabled and supported. Stopping a video releases its current player item. Network and system media frameworks may buffer content or maintain caches as part of playback.

“Wipe local data now” first stops receiving and playback, then clears the queue, pairing, timer and app preferences, removes app-managed web data and URL caches, and attempts to delete the app’s cache-directory contents. The interface returns to onboarding. Cleanup may take a short time and displays progress. If file cleanup fails, the app reports that some cached files may remain rather than claiming full success.

Wipe is an app-level reset, not certified forensic erasure. It cannot delete data in another device’s browser, clipboard, screenshot, shared message, provider account, router, OS diagnostic record or existing backup. Another browser may retain previously displayed titles or form input. Stop sharing and clear that browser independently if needed. Uninstalling Still removes its normal app container under iOS rules; restoring a backup may restore older preferences.

sections.heading: 8. Support, rights and safeguards
sections.body:
A support summary is generated only when you choose to share it. It contains the app version, OS version and generic receiver/playback status. It excludes your receiver name, Wi-Fi address, token, media URLs and titles. Review the system sharing destination yourself. No support report is automatically uploaded.

Depending on applicable law, you may have rights concerning information you voluntarily provide to the developer or a service provider. Contact the developer through the profile above for developer-held communications, and contact the relevant provider for provider-held playback data. Because Still has no account or telemetry database, it cannot identify or delete a server-side playback record that it never received. Provide only information necessary for your request.

Access tokens and input validation reduce accidental exposure but cannot guarantee perfect security. Report a suspected issue privately through available developer contact channels when possible. Avoid placing private credentials in public issues.

sections.heading: 9. Children, international services and policy changes
sections.body:
Still is a general-purpose playback tool and does not knowingly collect children’s personal information for developer telemetry. A parent or guardian should supervise content access, network sharing and use of third-party services where appropriate. Follow provider age requirements and applicable local rules.

Choosing online media or an external support site may involve service providers operating in other countries. Still does not upload analytics. An optional screen-sharing connection or TURN service may operate internationally; choose its operator knowingly. Policies of those providers govern their processing.

Future versions may change preferences or features. Material changes to this policy will be reflected in the bundled text and its effective/version information. This release contains no consent switch that secretly enables telemetry. Offline copies let you review the policy shipped with your installed version, even if the repository later changes.

sections.heading: 10. Optional whole-screen connections
sections.body:
Screen-sharing mode uses the HTTPS connection service configured on the receiving device. The developer supplies service source code but no hosted endpoint is preconfigured. The service exchanges a temporary room identifier, a private receiver-owner credential, an invitation credential, recording permission, session descriptions and ICE candidates. Session descriptions and candidates can reveal network addresses and device/media capabilities to the operator and the other peer. TLS protects signaling in transit to the operator; it does not hide these fields from that operator.

The supplied service keeps room state in memory, limits a session to two hours, retains a disconnected receiver briefly for reconnection, and clears room state when it ends or the process restarts. It adds no analytics or access-log feature. Infrastructure, reverse proxies, hosting providers or a customized deployment may create their own operational records. There is no promise that another operator follows this configuration.

WebRTC encrypts screen video in transit. Media travels directly between peers when possible; a configured TURN service can carry the encrypted media when network paths require it. The TURN operator can observe endpoints, timing and traffic volume. STUN services process network-discovery requests. These services are not automatically chosen from public providers in the supplied configuration. You decide which operator to trust; the app cannot guarantee anonymity, perfect security or connectivity on every network.

The Android companion uses the Android system screen-capture consent flow and an ongoing media-projection foreground service with a stop action. Android 13+ may request notification permission for its stop notification; if declined, use the app or Android’s active-app controls to stop. Desktop sending uses the browser’s screen picker. The sender can continue sharing while using other apps where its OS permits, but lock, revocation, battery policy or network changes can stop capture. Camera, microphone and system-audio capture are not implemented in this version. iPhone/iPad whole-screen sending is not implemented. A selected screen can reveal notifications, passwords or private messages; inspect what you share.

sections.heading: 11. Explicit local screen recordings
sections.body:
The receiver offers recording only for the WebRTC screen feed and only when the supplied sender has opted in before joining. Recording is off by default. A visible recording notice is sent to the sender. This consent control governs the supplied apps; it cannot prevent screenshots, external cameras, modified clients or other recording tools. Obtain any additional permission required by applicable law and by people whose information appears on screen.

Recordings contain screen video only, without audio. They are encoded as local MP4 files, with a 30-minute per-recording limit, bounded frame processing and a low-storage stop. Resolution is capped at a 1280-pixel long edge and the recording frame cadence is capped at 24 fps. Frames may be dropped to keep the player responsive. Protected content may be absent or black. This is not a YouTube downloader, stream-ripping tool or DRM bypass.

Saved recordings persist in Still’s application-support recordings folder until you delete or wipe them. The app marks that folder as excluded from backup; operating-system behavior and copies you export remain outside its control. A recording may include sensitive visible information. It is not automatically uploaded or saved to Photos. Sharing/exporting uses the system share sheet only after your action and needs no photo-library permission. Local Wipe deletes saved recordings after stopping and finalizing an active recording. Wipe cannot recall exported copies, provider records or existing backups. An interrupted save can leave a partial file; app startup attempts to remove incomplete recordings, and wipe removes the recordings folder.

sections.heading: 12. Background behavior
sections.body: On the receiving iPhone/iPad, local commands and WebRTC screen reception end when the app enters the background. Active screen recording stops and gets a bounded opportunity to finish saving. The audio background mode is used only for compatible native media playback, not silent audio or a background-server workaround. If you enable Background stream audio, native stream audio can continue under iOS rules. Native Picture in Picture can continue supported video playback after you start it through the player. YouTube is paused when the app backgrounds. iOS may interrupt, suspend or end any session; no setting guarantees indefinite operation.

sections.heading: In plain words
sections.body:
Use Still to watch video links you are entitled to use, on devices and networks you control or are authorized to use. Keep your pairing link private and expect the app to stay open while receiving. Still has no account or paid feature gate. It does not promise that every online video will play or that an iPhone becomes a certified Cast receiver.

These terms govern use of the app and local remote. The Store EULA governs the installed application license where distributed through a store. The Non-Commercial License governs the covered source and redistributions. Mandatory legal rights remain unaffected.

sections.heading: 2. What the app provides
sections.body:
Still receives supported media links and playback commands from its bundled browser remote or compatible clients over a local Wi-Fi network. It offers on-device playback, a temporary queue, appearance preferences and session controls. Its own Bonjour advertisement identifies its own protocol. It is not a certified Google Cast, AirPlay or Miracast receiver and uses its own WebRTC screen-sharing mode rather than those protocols.

The receiver must remain in the foreground. iOS can suspend networking, interrupt audio, restrict permissions or terminate the app. Backgrounding stops local commands and WebRTC screen reception. Native direct-stream audio may continue if enabled, and native Picture in Picture can continue where iOS permits it. YouTube pauses. These exceptions do not keep the receiver server alive. The current implementation uses IPv4 Wi-Fi pairing. Supported extensions, codecs, formats and controls are described in the bundled compatibility page and may change as Apple or media providers change their platforms.

sections.body:

Do not use Still to attack a network, harass another person, distribute malicious instructions or operate devices without authorization.

A source-code license for Still grants no rights to YouTube videos, music, thumbnails, marks or other third-party content.

sections.heading: 4. Local access and shared sessions
sections.body:
You decide when to start the receiver and who receives the pairing link. The link grants session access until revoked. A remote may see playback and queue information even in queue-only mode. Anyone you pair may submit unwanted links or choose disruptive actions within the selected access mode. Queue-only mode limits commands but does not verify that a submitted video is appropriate.

Use trusted Wi-Fi because remote traffic is local HTTP without transport encryption. Keep pairing credentials out of public posts and shared screenshots. Do not expose the receiver port to the public internet. Use Disconnect all remotes, Stop receiver or Local Wipe to revoke access. No setting guarantees protection against a person who can intercept or compromise your network or device.

sections.heading: 5. Providers, availability and controls
sections.body:
YouTube playback uses the official embedded player and remains subject to YouTube’s terms, API rules, advertising, availability and restrictions. Some videos cannot be embedded, require sign-in, need an on-device tap or are unavailable in your region. Still does not extract YouTube media URLs, download YouTube videos, strip provider advertisements or bypass controls.

Direct streams depend on their host, valid TLS certificates, supported codecs and valid URL access tokens. Live media may lack a duration or seekable range. Stream quality settings request a ceiling where variants exist; they do not create variants or force YouTube quality. Speed, volume and repeat can depend on provider and media support. A command being accepted means it was handed to the player, not that the provider has guaranteed successful playback.

Internet access, network costs and hardware are your responsibility. The developer is not responsible for a third party removing a video or changing its service. Provider and device rules can affect features without any change to this app’s source.

sections.heading: 6. Privacy and user-directed sharing
sections.body:
The bundled Privacy Policy explains zero developer telemetry, local preferences, temporary session state, provider requests and local wipe limits. Read it before sharing sensitive content. Still does not require a developer account or automatically upload viewing history or support diagnostics.

When you choose to share a pairing link, a support summary or a legal document, you select the destination in the system share sheet. Those destinations and any external links are independent services with their own rules. Do not include private media credentials in a public report. Local Wipe does not erase records held by those external services.

sections.heading: 11. Whole-screen sharing and recording
sections.body:
Optional screen sharing uses WebRTC with the configured connection service and, when necessary, a separately operated TURN relay. It supports the supplied Android sender and compatible desktop browsers, with screen video only. HTTPS hosting, relay bandwidth, sender consent and adequate connectivity are prerequisites. No hosted service, zero-latency transport, guaranteed reconnection or whole-screen compatibility with every device is included.

Only share screens you are authorized to share. The receiving app honors the sender’s opt-in before enabling its recording function. A sender can revoke sharing through its app or OS capture control. This does not prevent external capture or authorize recording of copyrighted or private material. Recordings are local files subject to deletion and export choices described in the Privacy Policy. You are responsible for obtaining any legally necessary consent. The developer does not promise forensic deletion or recovery of a failed recording.

The Android sender may use a visible, system-approved media-projection foreground service. The iOS receiver cannot continue as an arbitrary background server. Native media audio and Picture in Picture exceptions do not change that limitation. No user instruction or app setting overrides OS permissions, protected-content controls or network outages.

sections.heading: At a glance
sections.body:
Developer telemetry: none. Account: none. Preconfigured developer cloud service: none. Optional screen sharing: configured connection/TURN service. Automatic persistent watch history: none. Explicit screen recordings: local files until deleted. Preferences: on this device. Pairing and queue: memory only. Media playback: connects to the provider you choose. Local remote: HTTP on trusted Wi-Fi.

“Instant” describes stopping playback and revoking pairing immediately when you confirm a wipe. Removing web data and cache files is asynchronous and may take a short time. Still shows progress and reports cleanup errors. This is an app reset, not a certified secure-erasure product.

sections.heading: 1. What stays where
sections.body:
On this device, Still retains appearance and playback preferences, screen name, privacy choices, background stream-audio choice, configured screen-sharing server address and onboarding status. Explicit screen recordings persist as local MP4 files until deleted or wiped. While running it holds the video link, title, queue, temporary pairing credential and player state in memory. Its timer is a temporary deadline. Playback frameworks and web views may create buffers and caches as part of normal operation.

On a paired sender, the browser can display current and queued titles, video errors and control state. The sender may retain pasted text, browser history, screenshots or clipboard content outside Still’s control. On a media host, provider/network records are subject to that provider’s policy. Still does not have a developer server receiving a duplicate of your queue or playback history.

sections.heading: 2. Three different reset actions
sections.body:
Stop receiver closes receiving and revokes the current pairing token; it does not delete your preferences or necessarily stop a video already playing on the receiving screen. Disconnect all remotes revokes the token and restarts receiving with a new code while leaving your video in place. Wipe local data now stops both receiving and playback, empties the queue, cancels the timer and resets app-owned data, saved screen recordings and preferences.

Queue-only remotes restrict other devices to adding videos, but do not revoke their session or hide queue titles. Turning YouTube off blocks new YouTube loads, stops an active YouTube player and removes queued YouTube links; it is not a full app wipe. Pick the smallest action that fits what you want to do.

sections.heading: 3. What the wipe does
sections.body:
After your confirmation, Still first cancels the sleep timer, stops its network listener, closes remote connections and discards its session credential and activity time. It pauses and releases the player item, stops the embedded web page and clears the current video and queue. The app releases its request to keep your display awake.

It then requests deletion of web data from its active transient web store and the app’s default web store, clears the shared URL response cache, and attempts to remove files in its own cache directory. It waits for any active screen recording to finalize, deletes saved recordings, removes the app’s persistent preference domain, restores default playback settings and rebuilds its interface to discard form text and sheet state. You return to the welcome screen. Bundled legal pages, the app binary and installed assets remain so the app still works offline.

The app does not traverse arbitrary personal documents or delete content from other apps. It requests no photo, contact, microphone or file-library permission for this action. An error in cache-file removal is surfaced as a partial-cleanup message; stopping and revoking access has already happened.

sections.heading: 4. What it cannot wipe
sections.body:
Still cannot delete another device’s browser content, clipboard, shared pairing message, screenshots or downloads. It cannot erase video-provider logs, router records, Apple diagnostics, network-operator records, existing device backups or data you copied elsewhere. A disconnected browser may continue to display previously received text until you close or clear it.

Removing files through iOS APIs does not guarantee overwriting physical flash storage. The operating system may manage snapshots, system media caches or backups outside the app’s direct control. Restoring a backup can restore earlier preferences. For device disposal, use Apple’s device-reset guidance rather than relying on an app-level wipe.

sections.heading: 5. Safer sharing and recovery
sections.body:
Only pair on Wi-Fi you trust. Keep the full pairing link private. Queue-only mode can reduce disruption when friends send videos; it does not encrypt local traffic. A fresh start creates a new token, and a previously copied link will stop working. If you believe a link has leaked, disconnect all remotes or stop receiving immediately.

If a wipe reports partial cleanup, try again after a restart or uninstall Still to remove its normal container under iOS rules. Configure your OS backup and diagnostics choices separately. If you need support, use the safe summary and inspect its destination before sharing. The summary does not contain a pairing code, media URL, title, network address or your screen name.

sections.heading: 6. Offline access and verification
sections.body:
All legal, privacy, compatibility and connection-help text is packaged with the app, and can be read and searched without contacting a server. Theme selection, local wipe and local settings do not require an internet account. Online playback still needs the chosen provider; the existence of offline policies does not mean video streaming is offline.

The source repository includes the receiver protocol, tests and release-validation notes. Review those when evaluating the app’s privacy claims. “Zero telemetry” is a statement about developer collection implemented in this version, not a promise that Apple or every third-party media host processes no information. For details, read the full bundled Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 7. Screen sharing, recordings and wipe
sections.body:
Whole-screen connections use the configured service and optional STUN/TURN operators, who process connection metadata. Invitations are private bearer credentials. Owner credentials are not included in the sender invitation. Explicitly ending a session requests room revocation; if a device loses connectivity before that request arrives, the supplied service expires disconnected room state after a short grace period and sessions after two hours. Previously delivered data cannot be recalled.

Wipe stops screen receiving and recording as well as the local link receiver. It waits for any active recording to finish, then attempts to remove the recordings directory. If removal fails, it reports that some data may remain. It cannot delete the operator’s independent logs, another device’s state, or exported recordings. Saved recordings are excluded from backup by the app but are still sensitive local files until removed. App-level reset is not physical flash overwrite.

sections.heading: 1. Start on this screen
sections.body: Connect your iPhone or iPad to Wi-Fi. Open Still and tap Start receiver. Allow Local Network access if iOS asks. Keep Still open.

sections.heading: 2. Scan from the other device
sections.body: Put your other phone, tablet or computer on the same Wi-Fi. Scan Still’s QR code using that device’s camera. If scanning is difficult, use Share pairing link or expand Can’t scan the code? to copy the complete link.

sections.heading: 3. Send a video
sections.body: In YouTube, choose Share → Copy link. Open the paired browser remote, paste the link and press Play now. Direct HTTPS media links work too. Add to queue keeps the current video playing. If queue-only mode is on, remotes can add videos while playback remains under this screen’s control.

sections.heading: If it will not connect
sections.body: Keep Still open and check that both devices use the same Wi-Fi. In iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network, allow Still. Guest networks, VPNs, captive portals, browser HTTPS-only settings and router isolation can block local pairing. Start again after a Wi-Fi change and scan the new code. Local pairing uses HTTP, so use trusted Wi-Fi.

sections.heading: If a video will not play
sections.body: Try another video to distinguish a bad source from a connection issue. YouTube videos may block embedding, require sign-in or need a tap on the receiver’s player. Use Open original when available. Streams need supported codecs, valid HTTPS certificates and an unexpired URL. Check that YouTube playback has not been turned off in Privacy & Data.

sections.heading: Keep it simple
sections.body: The everyday flow is Start → Scan → Play. Settings is optional. Try a sleep timer for bedtime or queue-only remotes when friends are choosing videos. Stop receiver ends remote access. Wipe local data resets the app when you want to start fresh.

sections.heading: Devices and pairing
sections.body: iPhone and iPad with iOS/iPadOS 17 or later. Local IPv4 Wi-Fi and modern sender browsers. Local-command and whole-screen receivers stay open in the foreground. Compatible native streams can use audio background mode or native Picture in Picture; this does not keep the receivers alive. Bonjour announces Still’s own service; it does not create a YouTube Cast target.

sections.heading: Video sources
sections.body: YouTube watch, youtu.be, Shorts and live-video links that allow embedding. Direct HTTPS MP4, MOV, M4V, MP3, M4A and HLS (.m3u8) URLs with iOS-compatible codecs. Query-string access tokens are supported. Playlist pages, arbitrary web pages, custom authenticated headers and local HTTP media are not supported.

sections.heading: Playback and session tools
sections.body: Play/pause, seeking where supported, player volume, native stream full screen, queue of up to 20 items, queue editing, auto-next, repeat current video, supported playback speeds, skip intervals, HLS quality ceilings, session sleep timer and queue-only remotes. YouTube quality is managed by YouTube. Live media may lack a seekable timeline. Native Picture in Picture is available through supported stream-player controls, and background stream audio is optional. Still provides no background receiver service.

sections.heading: Privacy and personalization
sections.body: Five adaptive color themes, system/light/dark appearance, compact spacing, optional supported-device haptics, screen-awake setting, YouTube playback switch, zero developer telemetry, offline legal search, safe user-shared support summary and local wipe.

sections.heading: Unavailable protocols
sections.body: No certified Google Cast receiver, YouTube Cast-menu discovery, AirPlay receiving, Miracast, iPhone/iPad whole-screen sending, DRM bypass, YouTube downloading, public exposure of the local HTTP command server or IPv6-only local-link pairing. Optional WebRTC screen-sharing invitations can work over the internet with deployed HTTPS and TURN services. No promise that all provider videos support embedding, speed, seeking or quality changes.

sections.heading: Whole-screen video
sections.body: Android 10+ with the Still Sender companion and system capture consent; compatible desktop browsers using HTTPS getDisplayMedia. WebRTC video-only reception, adaptive quality profiles, bounded reconnect attempts and opt-in local video recording. Internet sharing needs a deployed connection service, valid HTTPS and usually TURN. Android and desktop capture may continue while other apps are used, under OS rules. Receiving on iPhone/iPad remains foreground only. No remote input/control of the source device, microphone, system audio, iPhone/iPad sending or guaranteed playback of protected content.

sections.heading: 1. One-time connection setup
sections.body: The app distributor or your administrator deploys the included HTTPS connection service and a TURN relay, then configures the service address in Still → Settings → Screen sharing. No hosted service is preconfigured in this source project. If you run your own service, use the repository deployment guide and a domain with a valid TLS certificate. This setup is required before normal users can receive an invitation.

sections.heading: 2. Invite a screen
sections.body: On the receiving iPhone/iPad, choose Receive a whole screen, then Create an invitation. Share or scan the invitation on the sending device. Keep the invitation private. It allows one sending device per session. Starting screen mode stops the local link receiver and its current video to keep the two modes clear.

sections.heading: 3. Share from Android or a computer
sections.body: On Android, install the Still Sender companion, open the invitation from the browser’s Open Android sender button or paste the full link into the companion. Choose a quality profile and whether recording is allowed, then choose a screen in Android’s permission dialog. On a supported computer browser, open the invitation, choose a profile and press Choose a screen. Your browser shows its own screen picker. iPhone/iPad whole-screen sending is not supported in this release.

sections.heading: 4. Record only with permission
sections.body: The sender must allow recording before joining; it is off by default. On the receiver, Record this screen stores video-only MP4 locally, without audio. The sender sees a recording notice. Stop & save finalizes it. Recordings are capped at 30 minutes and stop when storage is low. Find, preview, share or delete recordings in Settings → Recordings. Local Wipe deletes them. External screen capture cannot be prevented by this consent setting.

sections.heading: 5. Nearby, distant and interrupted connections
sections.body: The same invitation flow works nearby or across networks when the configured services can establish a WebRTC path. Congested Wi-Fi, mobile networks, firewalls, VPNs and long distances affect quality and delay. Try Lighter connection if needed. Both clients make bounded reconnection attempts after interruptions. Restart the invitation if recovery fails. The supplied service limits sessions to two hours and briefly preserves room state after a receiver disconnect.

sections.heading: 6. Background and stop controls
sections.body: The Android sender uses a visible foreground media-projection service, and desktop capture can continue while another app is used where the sender OS allows it. Android lock or OS policies can revoke capture. The iPhone/iPad receiver must remain open for whole-screen receiving and recording. Backgrounding it ends screen sharing and saves any active recording if the OS gives time. Separate direct-stream playback may use native Picture in Picture or optional background audio; neither keeps screen receiving alive.

sections.heading: 7. Privacy and source restrictions
sections.body: Screen video only is sent in this release. No camera, microphone, system audio or remote control of the sender. Notifications and private text visible on the selected screen can be exposed. Protected video can appear black, and provider restrictions are not bypassed. Signaling/TURN operators process connection metadata; WebRTC encrypts media in transit. Read the full bundled Privacy Policy and trust the configured service operator.
